title: Current Authority — Multi-Framework Implementation Bridge

core_distinction.statement: Historical instruction, approval, identity, or execution state is not automatically current authority for a new consequential action or result.
core_distinction.implementation_goal: Preserve truthful history while re-evaluating present authority at the consequential boundary and keeping explicit retry/resubmit attributable as fresh authority.

why_this_matters_for_ai_systems: AI agents increasingly resume, retry, migrate, delegate, recover, and execute tools across time and runtimes.
Without a current-authority boundary, cancelled instructions, stale approvals, delayed results, or resumed tool calls can silently act as if old authority were still live.
A shared implementation rule across frameworks reduces duplicate side effects, stale-action replay, and authority drift while preserving audit history.

live_framework_routes.verified_change: Two disjoint Qwen execution paths now have source-confirmed cancellation/history gaps. #13487 independently confirmed the Hosted Harness tool-profile path after Nakagawa-master opened the split verification issue.
live_framework_routes.next_target: Receiver-owned failing regression and narrow fix that preserves historical truth while preventing cancelled actionable context from becoming fresh authority.
live_framework_routes.larger_effect_if_achieved: Current-authority semantics become embedded in a major agent/runtime codebase across more than one internal execution path.

live_framework_routes.verified_change: Independent reproduction showed one logical tool action can produce duplicate provider writes after timeout and resume. A Nakagawa-bound control separated logical identity, attempt identity, and current authority.
live_framework_routes.next_target: Framework-visible cross-invocation re-execution signal, regression, documentation, or equivalent upstream acceptance that makes resumed work distinguishable from first execution.
live_framework_routes.larger_effect_if_achieved: Durable/recoverable agent graphs gain a portable boundary between replay semantics and present authority for consequential external actions.

live_framework_routes.verified_change: AutoGen is actively designing common guardrail/approval interception around tool execution, with identity, digest, approval, audit, and single-use concepts already under discussion.
live_framework_routes.next_target: Add or test the distinct rule that a historically valid ALLOW is not a durable execution lease after delay, cancellation, restart, recovery, role revocation, or policy change.
live_framework_routes.larger_effect_if_achieved: Current-authority revalidation can become a reusable guardrail primitive across many AutoGen tools rather than a one-off bug fix.

public_reuse_rule.allowed: Independent verification, falsification, regression design, implementation, focused review, or non-fit analysis using each participant's own current permissions.
public_reuse_rule.provenance: If this bridge materially informs a result, preserve the Nakagawa Master source relationship. If the distinction was independently rediscovered before seeing this bridge, state that instead.

evidence_boundary: This bridge routes public, bounded implementation opportunities. It does not claim merge, release, operational use, endorsement, or broad adoption unless the linked receiver-owned evidence establishes that stage.
